In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
NGC 6240 is an ultraluminous IR galaxy with a starburst nucleus and a supermassive black hole.
NGC 6240 is not a typical ultraluminous IR galaxy, but a starburst galaxy with a superposition of a Seyfert nucleus.
NGC 6240 and NGC 253 show similar plasma properties, but the former is much more luminous in X-rays and the latter has a much higher star-formation rate.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Fe K line emission in NGC 6240 is due to reflection of the nuclear X-ray continuum from optically thick material in the circumnuclear region, as well as to collisionally ionized plasmas.
the XMM-Newton spectrum of the ULIR NGC 6240 is dominated by a collisionally ionized plas ma component, which is distributed in a similar way as the hot plasma in the starburst galaxy NGC253.
the neutral and ionized Fe K line emission is due to reflection of X-rays from the central engine off optically thick material.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the neutral Fe K and the ionized Fe lines can be used to probe the properties of the circumnuclear material in active galax ies and starburst galaxies.
the Fe K line emission in the local starbursts is not necessarily due to reflection.
the Fe Kline emission from NGC 6240 can be successfully model led as a combination of reflection from optically thick matter and emission from collisionally ionized plasmas.
